# Species | Verdict | Priority (1 = first pass, 2 = second pass, 3 = monitor) | Design review
VENUSAUR|Keep|3|110 Sp. Atk, Sleep Powder, Leech Seed and Synthesis already make this a complete Grass/Poison attacker or tank. Chlorophyll and Thick Fat are alternative builds, so it does not get sun Speed and Fire/Ice mitigation together. Preserve current stats and coverage; do not add another setup tool merely to match Charizard.
CHARIZARD|Watch|2|Fire/Dragon removes the old quadruple Rock weakness; Levitate can remove Ground while Drought powers Fire and supports teammates. Those abilities are alternatives. Keep 535 BST initially; test Drought with Weather Ball and Roost, and Dragon Dance physical sets separately. If sun teams dominate, adjust weather access before reducing Charizard's stats.
BLASTOISE|Nerf timing|1|Water/Steel, Shell Smash at level 35 and either Drizzle or Mega Launcher put unusually much into one starter. Move its own Shell Smash from 35 to 50, and audit Squirtle/Wartortle retention so the restriction is real. Preserve 535 BST, Flash Cannon and the ability choices; recheck postgame Smash sets before any further nerf.
BUTTERFREE|Keep|3|90 Speed and 110 Sp. Atk with Quiver Dance, sleep, recovery and either Tinted Lens or Compound Eyes already solve its traditional weakness. Tinted Lens does not also raise Sleep Powder accuracy. Retain its 60/45 physical frailty and Rock weakness; a further Speed or bulk buff would remove useful counterplay.
BEEDRILL|Keep|3|115 Attack, 95 Speed, Adaptability, U-turn and Drill Run give it a real offensive niche. Swords Dance is available but physical Defense remains 40. Keep those weaknesses and its current timing. Do not add Tough Claws or further raise Speed without first testing Adaptability Poison Jab/X-Scissor against the same opponents as Crobat.
PIDGEOT|Keep|3|115 Sp. Atk and No Guard Hurricane plus Heat Wave already create a distinct special bird. Hurricane arrives at 50, so its peak is delayed naturally. Keep current stats and timing; use its vulnerability to enemy accurate attacks and its lack of strong boosting as costs for reliable Hurricane.
RATICATE|Watch|3|113 Speed and 97 Attack are already a major redesign. Guts plus an orb and Facade can be much stronger than BST 460 suggests; Technician and Hustle are separate options. Keep initially, but test orb Facade after Mahogany item access. If excessive, lower Speed 113 to 105 rather than gutting all three abilities.
FEAROW|Keep|3|110 Attack, 115 Speed and Intimidate give it a fast physical niche beside special Pidgeot and recoil-focused Dodrio. Sniper is an alternative offensive route. Preserve current stats, Drill Peck and Roost; do not add another major damage ability or boosting move until ordinary physical bird matchups justify it.
ARBOK|Keep|3|Poison/Dark, 110 Attack and Intimidate or Strong Jaw already give it meaningful defensive and offensive roles. Its single typing weakness is Ground before ability interactions, but bulk and Speed are moderate. Keep current design; preserve its lack of effortless recovery instead of inflating BST to match newer Poison/Dark species.
SANDSLASH|Keep|3|100 Attack and 110 Defense with Rapid Spin, rocks and Sand Rush make this a useful sand cleaner or utility Ground. Sand Force is a separate wallbreaking option. Keep stats; compare against Excadrill with equal sand turns and items before any buff. Its non-Steel typing and defensive utility must be part of that comparison.
NIDOQUEEN|Keep|3|90/87/85 bulk and Sheer Force coverage distinguish it from Nidoking without requiring equal Sp. Atk. Hazards provide a useful alternative to four attacks. Preserve its current stats, types and abilities; account for Sheer Force with Life Orb before considering extra special offense or recovery.
NIDOKING|Keep|3|90 Sp. Atk can look modest, but Sheer Force and broad special coverage compensate strongly; 102 Attack also permits physical alternatives. Keep current stats. Compare the Life Orb special set against Nidoqueen rather than comparing BST alone, and retain the Speed/bulk distinction between the pair.
CLEFABLE|Watch|2|Magic Guard, Unaware, recovery, Wish and broad coverage create several excellent sets, but Magic Guard and Unaware never coexist. Keep its moderate 480 BST. Test long games, Calm Mind and Wish teams separately; if stalling is excessive, restrict a utility route or recovery PP globally rather than removing both defining abilities.
NINETALES|Keep|3|Fire/Fairy, 109 Speed, Drought and Nasty Plot are already a substantial niche. 81 Sp. Atk is deliberately lower than Sunflora or Charizard; sun damage compensates. Keep its stats and avoid raising Sp. Atk simply because it is low on paper. Flash Fire is custom and deserves separate testing.
WIGGLYTUFF|Buff|2|Magic Guard and Wish justify its high HP, but 55 Defense is a severe bottleneck on a 140-HP support Pokémon. Raise Defense 55 to 65 (+10 BST, 495 total), leaving Sp. Def 60 and Speed 55 intact. Keep its broad coverage and Nasty Plot; this is a small physical resilience buff, not a second Clefable redesign.
VILEPLUME|Keep|3|110 Sp. Atk, two recovery options, sleep and Poison Puppeteer already support offense or disruptive defense. Chlorophyll is an alternative to the poison/confusion build. Keep stats and typing. Test repeated poison/confusion pressure under the game's confusion rules before expanding its move support or recovery.
PARASECT|Keep|3|The actual Enhanced typing is Bug/Ghost, with 85 HP, 115 Attack, 100 Defense, Spore and Regenerator as one option. This is already a strong rescue of the species. Keep 30 Speed as meaningful counterplay; do not grant fast sleep or boost all its bulk. Tough Claws is an alternative, not an extra multiplier.
VENOMOTH|Nerf movepool|1|Bug/Psychic with sleep, Quiver Dance, Tinted Lens and recovery is powerful enough on its own. Remove Baton Pass from every acquisition route in this family, preserving Quiver Dance and its ability choices. The target is passing a multi-stat boost after sleep, not its viability as an independent sweeper.
DUGTRIO|Watch|2|Arena Trap can decide matchups despite only 35 HP. Keep its low bulk and 100 Attack initially; do not buff by BST. Test grounded targets with Ghost escape and switching rules respected. If trapping is too deterministic, replace Arena Trap with Hyper Cutter; leave the sand options and Speed intact.
PERSIAN|Keep|3|90 Attack, 80 Sp. Atk, 115 Speed and Technician support mixed utility and a distinct fast Normal role. Fake Out and coverage matter more than its BST. Keep stats and current Nasty Plot access. Alolan Persian's Fur Coat is an alternative form niche, not a reason to give regular Persian equal physical durability.
GOLDUCK|Keep|3|Water/Psychic, 95 Sp. Atk, Nasty Plot and either Swift Swim or Cloud Nine already offer offense and weather control. Keep its balanced stats. Swift Swim needs outside rain and cannot also suppress weather. Its role should be measured against Kingdra in rain and Lanturn for utility rather than increased reflexively.
ARCANINE|Keep|3|555 BST, Intimidate, ExtremeSpeed, recovery and broad mixed coverage are already generous. Defiant and the custom Flash Fire are alternatives. Preserve current stats and avoid adding boosting moves. Compare its sustainable Intimidate set against the Hisuian form's stronger recoil-free attacks before making either form better.
POLIWRATH|Keep|3|Belly Drum, priority, Water/Fighting and either Iron Fist or Swift Swim create viable offense despite 95 Attack. Water Absorb gives a separate defensive role. Keep stats and timing; test Drum with available Berries before granting more Attack or Speed. Its special-defense advantage over offensive Fighting rivals matters.
ALAKAZAM|Watch|3|135 Sp. Atk, 120 Speed, Nasty Plot, Recover and Magic Guard already make an elite special sweeper. Keep physical frailty and existing numbers. Life Orb or Focus Sash variants should be tested separately where the item is obtainable; do not add bulk because it cannot safely set up against physical attackers.
MACHAMP|Keep|3|130 Attack, No Guard DynamicPunch and Guts with an orb give distinct strong sets. The game's confusion chance makes DynamicPunch especially disruptive. Keep low Speed as its cost; no Attack buff is needed. Check actual DynamicPunch access in campaign teams before blaming a whole species for an early boss spike.
VICTREEBEL|Keep|3|Mixed 105/100 offenses, Chlorophyll, sleep and recovery already make this threatening in sun. Poison Puppeteer is a separate disruption build. Keep stats and coverage. Assess both physical and special four-move sets rather than treating every listed move as simultaneously usable or multiplying both ability benefits.
TENTACRUEL|Keep|3|100 Speed, 120 Sp. Def, Rapid Spin, Toxic Spikes, Flip Turn and Scald give it a full utility role. Merciless can punish poison but competes with Rain Dish/Clear Body. No stat buff is needed. Preserve its weaker physical Defense so fast hazard control does not also become an effortless physical wall.
GOLEM|Keep|3|120 Attack, 130 Defense, Sturdy and hazards already produce an honest slow physical role. Water/Grass weaknesses keep it from universal use. Keep stats and ability choices; improve a specific boss or encounter's move timing only if campaign testing shows an actual gap. Do not erase both quadruple weaknesses to solve every bad matchup.
RAPIDASH|Keep|3|115 Speed, 105 Attack, recovery and Reckless are substantial improvements. Flash Fire has a custom stat-boosting effect and is another strong route. Keep its 65 HP and current physical offense. Galarian Rapidash has a different Enhanced typing, so compare coverage and immunities rather than demanding identical performance.
SLOWBRO|Watch|2|Unaware or Regenerator with Slack Off and substantial Defense can dominate physical setup teams. They are separate abilities. Keep 490 BST, but test prolonged switching and recovery with item access equalized. If wall cores become tedious, address recovery economy or trainer coverage before reducing Slowbro's defining physical Defense.
DODRIO|Keep|3|110 Attack/Speed, Reckless, Swords Dance and Roost already form a strong physical bird. Frail special bulk and recoil keep it distinct from Fearow and Staraptor. Keep current stats; avoid another Speed increase. Test Swords Dance with a real four-move limit so recovery and coverage carry their proper opportunity costs.
DEWGONG|Keep|3|110 HP, 80 Speed and three useful ability routes already improve this substantially. Snow Warning offers team utility; Swift Swim needs a different team. Keep stats and priority access. Hail is not modern snow, so no automatic Ice Defense boost should be assumed when judging its survivability.
MUK|Keep|3|Regenerator on 105 HP/100 Sp. Def and Toxic Spikes makes this a useful defensive Poison. Poison Touch and Sticky Hold trade that recovery for other roles. Keep current stats; avoid adding direct recovery as well as Regenerator. Alolan Muk has superior typing but a different set of ability tradeoffs.
CLOYSTER|Watch|1|Skill Link plus Shell Smash and physical multi-hit STAB is an obvious sweep candidate despite 45 Sp. Def. Keep its stats until tested against priority, special attackers and sturdy counterplay. If campaign Smash sweeps recur, delay Smash or multi-hit access, auditing Shellder inheritance, before lowering Defense or crippling Skill Link.
GENGAR|Keep|3|130 Sp. Atk, 110 Speed, Nasty Plot and Levitate already give premium offense. Merciless is a different poison-team set. Keep its current physical frailty, and test whether opposing AI carries actual answers. There is no reason to restore an extra weakness or buff stats based on its low 500 BST.
HYPNO|Watch|2|No Guard makes Hypnosis, DynamicPunch and Zap Cannon extremely disruptive, offsetting its modest offenses. Bad Dreams is a separate sleep-payoff choice. Do not raise Sp. Atk until those sets are tested. If reliable sleep proves oppressive, replace No Guard with Frisk rather than simultaneously buffing offense and retaining perfect control.
KINGLER|Keep|3|130 Attack and either Tough Claws or Sheer Force give plenty of damage; Swords Dance exists. Keep weaker special bulk and 75 Speed as costs. Verify which Water move actually triggers the chosen ability instead of applying both bonuses or assuming every attack has a removable secondary effect.
ELECTRODE|Keep|3|150 Speed and Recover provide unusually strong longevity for fast support; 90 Sp. Atk is adequate with pivoting and disruption. Keep current numbers. Do not add Nasty Plot to make it a second fast sweeper. Compare its utility against Hisuian Electrode before changing the latter's offensive stats.
EXEGGUTOR|Keep|3|125 Sp. Atk, sleep, recovery, Chlorophyll or Harvest already make this powerful when supported. Keep low Speed outside sun and its multiple weaknesses. Do not fill the empty ability slot with another large offensive boost merely to have three unique abilities; empty slots fall back to the first ability.
MAROWAK|Keep|3|425 BST is misleading because Thick Club doubles Attack, and Technician further rewards appropriate moves on its own build. Swords Dance/Belly Drum add setup. Keep current Attack and low Speed; evaluate item-boosted Bonemerang before any buff. Thick Club availability matters more than matching other Ground species' BST.
HITMONLEE|Keep|3|120 Attack, 92 Speed and Reckless or Unburden already make strong offensive alternatives. Priority and utility coverage reduce dependence on raw Speed. Keep stats; Unburden should be evaluated only with a consumable item that actually activates in this engine. Its poor Defense remains a fair weakness.
HITMONCHAN|Keep|3|75 HP and 110 Sp. Def, Iron Fist drain/priority punches and Scrappy as an alternative give it a useful balanced Fighting niche. Keep 105 Attack and 81 Speed. Ensure the punch membership table is used when assessing coverage; not every Fighting move receives Iron Fist.
WEEZING|Keep|3|120 Defense, burns and either Levitate or Neutralizing Gas provide excellent physical disruption. Gas can disable enemy weather/damage abilities but also changes field interactions. Keep its lack of strong direct recovery. Test Gas against the same boosted attackers as Levitate rather than assuming both effects coexist.
KANGASKHAN|Watch|1|Parental Bond already uses a quarter-strength second hit, so recommending that as a new nerf would be redundant. The remaining concern is duplicated on-hit effects, Substitute breaking, drain and priority. Keep stats provisionally and test actual multi-hit outcomes. If still excessive, replace hidden Parental Bond with Tough Claws while retaining Scrappy.
SEAKING|Keep|3|This is already a special-leaning redesign with 102 Sp. Atk, 78 Speed, Scald and Flip Turn. Lightning Rod can turn an Electric switch-in into special pressure; Swift Swim is separate. Keep current stats. Its physical 75 Attack makes Megahorn coverage optional rather than justification for another large physical buff.
STARMIE|Watch|3|115 Speed, Recover and Regenerator give it unusually safe fast utility; Analytic and Natural Cure are alternative builds. Keep stats and test Regenerator with Rapid Spin and attacking coverage. If it crowds out Tentacruel, first compare poison utility and physical bulk rather than giving every Water spinner Regenerator.
PINSIR|Keep|3|125 Attack, 100 Defense, Swords Dance and Guts/Moxie/Mold Breaker give several valid physical builds. Keep pure Bug and 85 Speed as tradeoffs. A Flying retype or extra damage ability would overlap heavily with already powerful physical Bugs. Test individual sets before trying to raise its BST.
TAUROS|Keep|3|100 Attack, 110 Speed and Intimidate or Sheer Force give a strong fast Normal without setup overload. Keep stats. Sheer Force should be evaluated with actual qualifying moves and item synergy; physical Normal attacks do not all receive that boost. The Paldean forms trade Speed and typing for greater physical bulk.
GYARADOS|Keep|3|125 Attack, Dragon Dance, Intimidate or Moxie and 100 Sp. Def already make this excellent. Keep the Electric weakness and 81 Speed before setup. Its empty second slot is not a gameplay defect. No additional coverage or stat buff is needed until opponents demonstrate consistent, fair counters.
LAPRAS|Keep|3|130 HP, Water Absorb or rain-supported Hydration and Ice coverage give substantial defensive utility. Dragon Dance is a separate offensive experiment, not a reason to buff Attack to 110. Keep 535 BST and current priority. Test against other bulky Waters with Freeze-Dry and recovery limitations respected.
DITTO|Keep|3|Imposter determines viability rather than 288 BST. Preserve its modest HP and restricted move access. Test transformed items, boosts and copied moves using the game's actual Transform rules. Increasing all six stats would mostly be wasted and could distort HP-based counterplay; do not add ordinary coverage or setup moves.
VAPOREON|Keep|3|130 HP, 110 Sp. Atk, Wish and immunity or rain recovery already support bulky Water teams. Keep stats; test Wish/Protect and Hydration/Rest as different sets. Its low physical Defense is the reason it does not replace every Water wall, and should remain a deliberate tradeoff.
JOLTEON|Keep|3|130 Speed, 110 Sp. Atk and Volt Absorb or Competitive are already sufficient. Quick Feet requires a status/item cost. Keep current stats and preserve its limited bulk. Evaluate late coverage with configurable Hidden Power included, because missing a native coverage move does not mean this game leaves it without that option.
FLAREON|Watch|2|110 HP, 130 Attack and 95 Speed are an enormous redistribution, especially with Guts, an orb, Facade and Flare Blitz. Keep its frail defenses provisionally; test both orb and custom Flash Fire builds. If it exceeds ordinary attackers, reduce HP 110 to 95 first (-15 BST), retaining its new Speed and offensive identity.
OMASTAR|Watch|2|115 Sp. Atk, 125 Defense, Shell Smash and Water/Rock STAB already offer strong setup with hazard alternatives. Swift Swim is an additional team route, not stacked with Weak Armor. Keep stats; if campaigns repeatedly collapse to Smash, delay access across Omanyte and Omastar instead of weakening every set.
KABUTOPS|Keep|3|115 Attack, Swift Swim or Tough Claws, Swords Dance and Aqua Jet are sufficient for a useful rain cleaner. Keep 80 Speed outside rain and special frailty. Compare it with Omastar as a physical alternative; avoid giving it recovery or extra weather-independent Speed merely to overcome its intended costs.
AERODACTYL|Watch|3|130 Speed with Dragon Dance, hazards and Roost is already generous. Rock Head or Strong Jaw change damage routes but do not stack. Keep current stats initially; a fast Dragon Dance set deserves testing before any Attack increase. Ordinary offensive frailty and the Rock typing's weaknesses still provide counterplay.
SNORLAX|Watch|2|160 HP, 110 Sp. Def, Belly Drum and Slack Off create a very complete bulky win condition. Keep Attack and HP initially; test Curse and Drum independently with actual Berry healing. If repeated recovery makes counterplay impractical, remove Slack Off from its own routes while preserving Rest and its classic tank identity.
ARTICUNO|Keep|3|Snow Warning and recovery make this valuable even though Ice/Flying has difficult weaknesses. Keep 580 BST and current Speed. Hail creates chip and Blizzard support but does not grant a modern snow Defense bonus. Evaluate hazard removal support before adding bulk or eliminating its signature typing drawbacks.
ZAPDOS|Keep|3|125 Sp. Atk, 100 Speed, recovery and Static or Lightning Rod already support elite offense and defense. Keep current stats and abilities. Ground immunity comes from Flying; Electric immunity only belongs to the Lightning Rod build. This is an upper benchmark for ordinary special birds, not a target every bird must match.
MOLTRES|Keep|3|125 Sp. Atk with recovery, Flame Body or Competitive makes a strong special bird. Preserve the Rock weakness as a team-building cost, especially without assuming Heavy-Duty Boots exist. Keep stats. Compare supported hazard-cleared sets against Zapdos and Articuno before trying to solve every unfavorable matchup with Speed.
DRAGONITE|Watch|3|Multiscale, Roost, Dragon Dance and tutor ExtremeSpeed already make a powerful pseudo-legendary. Keep current 600 BST and abilities. Test hazards and multi-hit attacks before calling Multiscale unanswerable; they affect full-HP protection. Its other abilities represent different sets rather than additional layers of the same build.
MEWTWO|Keep|3|680 BST, 154 Sp. Atk, 130 Speed, Nasty Plot and Recover belong to an intentionally exceptional legendary class. Keep current stats if acquisition is late and ordinary Tower/link rules restrict it appropriately. Do not use it as the power target for regular species. Audit availability separately from species balance.
MEW|Nerf|1|120 in all six stats gives 720 BST alongside extraordinary coverage, several setup paths, Baton Pass and Trace. Restore all six stats to 100 (600 BST), preserving versatility as its defining strength. This is the clearest numerical outlier; keep its broad movepool, then reassess boost passing under the same global policy as other species.
MEGANIUM|Keep|3|Grass/Fairy, 100/100 defenses, Leech Seed and three genuinely useful ability choices already make this a strong starter. Triage gives priority to healing/draining moves, whereas Mega Sol provides its own sun-like move benefits; they cannot combine. Keep 93 Sp. Atk. Avoid adding sleep or more bulk before comparing those separate builds.
TYPHLOSION|Watch|2|124 Sp. Atk, 101 Speed and Adaptability are already excellent for Fire offense, especially when paired with outside sun. Flash Fire offers a separate custom boosting route. Keep current numbers initially; test its strongest Fire attacks at realistic HP and PP before considering a nerf. It needs neither extra coverage nor another Speed buff.
FERALIGATR|Keep|3|Water/Dark, 110 Attack, Dragon Dance and either Strong Jaw or Sheer Force create complete physical offense. Aqua Jet provides a Speed-independent route. Keep 535 BST and the current move support. Judge bite and secondary-effect sets separately; its low special offense is an intentional specialization rather than wasted balance space.
FURRET|Keep|3|95 HP, 105 Speed, Fur Coat or Scrappy, ExtremeSpeed and pivoting already make a useful early Normal. Fur Coat does not also let Normal attacks hit Ghosts. Keep 85 Attack; avoid adding Swords Dance to this fast, physically resilient toolkit. Its low Sp. Def and limited damage abilities preserve fair weaknesses.
NOCTOWL|Keep|3|Psychic/Flying, 106 Sp. Atk, 116 Sp. Def, Roost and Tinted Lens or Intimidate offer real roles beside Pidgeot. Keep 60 Speed and 60 Defense. Nasty Plot plus resistance bypass is already threatening; a Speed buff would blur its bulky special-bird niche and reduce the costs of its offensive set.
LEDIAN|Keep|3|105 Attack, 95 Speed, Bug/Fighting, drain punches, Mach Punch and Roost already rescue it decisively. Technician and Iron Fist are alternatives. Keep stats; its inherited Quiver Dance is not a reason to raise 35 Sp. Atk. Test its physical priority set and Swords Dance passing separately before granting more bulk or damage.
ARIADOS|Keep|3|80 Speed, 110 Attack, Sticky Web, Toxic Spikes, priority and Merciless already create an offensive hazard niche. It is no longer the frail, slow original Ariados. Keep current stats and avoid stacking another status-enhancing ability. Assess poison-enabled critical hits against actual poison immunities and cleansing tools.
CROBAT|Keep|3|130 Speed, mixed options, Roost and Infiltrator make this broadly useful; Merciless adds a separate poison-team payoff. Keep stats. Fast support is enough to distinguish it from Beedrill, and a reliable new boosting route would narrow counterplay. Test poison support as a team cost rather than assuming every opponent starts poisoned.
LANTURN|Keep|3|125 HP, 96 Sp. Atk, Scald, Volt Switch, status utility and one of two absorption abilities form a complete pivot. Water Absorb and Volt Absorb never coexist. Keep 70 Defense and 67 Speed as costs; adding Recover or Regenerator would risk crowding out other bulky Water pivots.
XATU|Keep|3|95 Speed, 95 Sp. Atk, Roost and Magic Bounce provide a strong anti-status niche. Keep its modest defenses and stats, which distinguish it from Espeon and slower Noctowl. Native attacks plus Hidden Power supply enough offense. Improve an actual campaign access problem only if it is observed, rather than boosting stats automatically.
AMPHAROS|Keep|3|Electric/Dragon and 115 Sp. Atk already provide valuable resistances and offense. Galvanize Hyper Voice, Mold Breaker attacks or Static support are alternative builds, with Volt Switch for utility. Keep 55 Speed; Agility offers an investment-based route. Do not add both recovery and Speed to remove every cost of its bulky attacker role.
BELLOSSOM|Keep|3|Grass/Fairy, 95/100 defenses, Quiver Dance, Sleep Powder, recovery and Triage as an option already make this excellent. Triage priority drain is different from Chlorophyll's sun Speed. Keep stats. Test sleep plus Quiver Dance before advancing move timing or adding more coverage; its Fire/Poison/Steel matchups should still matter.
AZUMARILL|Watch|2|110 HP, Huge Power, Belly Drum and Aqua Jet are more important than the printed 50 Attack. Keep stats and avoid any Attack buff. Test Drum with obtainable Berries and priority blockers. If it sweeps too easily, reduce HP 110 to 100 first; Water/Fairy typing and Huge Power should remain its core identity.
SUDOWOODO|Keep|3|90 HP, 115 Attack, 125 Defense, Rock Head recoil moves, Body Press and Sucker Punch give meaningful physical utility. Keep very low Speed and Sp. Atk. Compare its recoil-free offense with Golem's Ground STAB rather than making both identical. Additional recovery would remove one of its important costs.
POLITOED|Keep|3|Drizzle makes a 500-BST Water valuable for an entire team, even without the strongest personal damage. Keep current stats and Damp/Water Absorb alternatives. Rain balance must include the sweepers it enables and the five/eight-turn duration, not only Politoed's damage. No further personal offense or recovery buff is necessary initially.
JUMPLUFF|Nerf movepool|1|Spore at level 64 combines perfect-accuracy sleep with 110 Speed, Encore, Leech Seed, Substitute and recovery. Remove Spore from Jumpluff and every inherited/tutor route; preserve Sleep Powder as its less reliable control option. Keep current stats and Chlorophyll. This retains the fast support identity while restoring a meaningful failure chance.
SUNFLORA|Keep|3|The runtime Enhanced typing is Grass/Fire, despite the Grass/Grass base-stat file. Drought, 125 Sp. Atk, Weather Ball, Earth Power and recovery already make it a strong slow sun specialist. Keep 30 Speed. Chlorophyll is an alternative needing external sun, so do not judge it as simultaneously self-setting weather and doubling Speed.
QUAGSIRE|Keep|3|Unaware, Recover, Water/Ground and 95 HP/Attack/Defense already produce a useful physical setup check. Keep low Speed and Sp. Def. Recovery arrives late by level-up, with campaign access considered separately. Do not remove the Grass weakness or give it universal special bulk to match newer Water walls.
ESPEON|Watch|3|130 Sp. Atk, 110 Speed, Magic Bounce, Morning Sun and Baton Pass make a versatile offensive support Pokémon. Keep stats and test boost passing under the shared Baton Pass recommendation. It should pay a four-move cost for recovery and support; do not add further coverage or bulk simply because other Psychics have more options.
UMBREON|Keep|3|95/110/130 bulk, Wish/Moonlight and Magic Guard already make a durable Dark support Pokémon. Keep very low damage and 65 Speed. Evaluate stall length with actual recovery PP and Wish use, but do not add stronger setup offense. Magic Guard is an alternative to Synchronize and Inner Focus, not an extra passive effect.
SLOWKING|Watch|2|110 Sp. Def, Slack Off and either Regenerator or Unaware already establish a special defensive role. Keep 490 BST and 30 Speed. Judge it against Slowbro with physical and special attackers separated; a universal bulk buff would erase their distinction. Test recovery cores before editing species stats.
UNOWN|Keep|3|This is already redesigned to 473 BST with 108 Sp. Atk, 85 Speed, Psychic, Calm Mind, Earth Power, Trick and Shadow Ball compatibility. Keep its intentionally narrow seven-move listed pool and Levitate/Analytic alternatives. Hidden Power can be tuned in this game, so it is not trapped with one random useless attack.
WOBBUFFET|Watch|1|190 HP, Shadow Tag, Encore and Counter/Mirror Coat can force highly deterministic exchanges without conventional attacks. Keep its restricted movepool and stats while testing real switch and Ghost escape rules. If oppressive, replace Shadow Tag with the implemented Pressure, preserving its reactive identity and restricted moves. Do not buff offenses.
FORRETRESS|Keep|3|140 Defense, Sturdy, three hazard types, Rapid Spin, Volt Switch and Body Press already make it excellent utility. Keep 40 Speed and 60 Sp. Def. A Fire weakness is a meaningful cost, not a defect to remove. Recovery or Regenerator would make hazard repetition much safer than its current role warrants.
STEELIX|Keep|3|200 Defense, 105 Attack, Body Press, hazards and Dragon Dance already give enough tools. Sturdy, Sand Force and Sheer Force are different builds. Keep 30 Speed and 65 Sp. Def; do not raise offensive stats just because Dragon Dance looks awkward. Its job includes checking physical attackers and setting field pressure.
GRANBULL|Keep|3|120 Attack, improved bulk, Intimidate or Strong Jaw, early Play Rough and even Lovely Kiss provide a real Fairy bruiser niche. Keep 45 Speed. Quick Feet trades Intimidate's safety for conditional Speed. Further Attack or priority would overcompensate for a weakness already mitigated by sleep and paralysis support.
SCIZOR|Watch|2|Technician Bullet Punch, Swords Dance, Roost and Bug/Steel on 130 Attack are already a complete offensive-defensive package. Keep stats initially; test priority after boosts with Fire checks and ability suppression present. Do not add stronger coverage or another damage ability. Baton Pass should follow the same shared rule as other setup passers.
SHUCKLE|Keep|3|Sticky Web and Stealth Rock with Sturdy already create a lead niche independent of its tiny offenses. Contrary Shell Smash is defensive, not a normal sweeping boost. Keep stats and restricted damage. Do not buff Attack or HP to match its 505 BST; low HP and passivity are the balancing costs of enormous defenses.
HERACROSS|Keep|3|125 Attack, Guts or Moxie, and Skill Link with appropriate multi-hit coverage offer strong alternatives. Keep 85 Speed and the Flying weakness. Test orb and Skill Link builds separately and respect hit counts. No further Attack buff is needed to make it compete with Breloom's priority/sleep identity.
MAGCARGO|Keep|3|75 HP, 150 Defense, 110 Sp. Atk, 100 Sp. Def, Recover and Shell Smash already make it heavily improved. Solid Rock halves quadruple-effective damage in this custom engine, further helping it. Keep 30 Speed and Fire/Rock; do not add more bulk just by recalling how weak original Magcargo was.
CORSOLA|Keep|3|115 in both defenses, Recover, Regenerator or Storm Drain, Scald and hazards already give this a strong support niche. Keep 65 HP and 35 Speed. Storm Drain and Regenerator are different builds. Its Water/Rock weaknesses and modest damage prevent it from replacing every Water wall; another recovery ability or bulk buff is unnecessary.
OCTILLERY|Keep|3|Water/Fire, 110 in both offenses, 95 Defense, pulses and Mega Launcher or Analytic already create a valuable slow mixed attacker. Keep 45 Speed. Mega Launcher boosts listed pulse moves rather than all Water/Fire attacks; compare the actual four-move set before adding more offense or a Speed-doubling ability.
DELIBIRD|Buff timing|2|110 Speed, 110 Sp. Atk, Prankster or Technician, hazard removal and Freeze-Dry already rescue its viability. Its relevant special Ice moves arrive at 34/36. Move its own Ice Beam from 36 to 28, leaving Freeze-Dry at 34 and stats unchanged. This improves midgame reliability without increasing its late-game ceiling.
MANTINE|Keep|3|140 Sp. Def, Roost, Water Absorb and Water/Flying give a complete special wall; Swift Swim is a separate offensive route. Keep 85 HP and 70 Defense. Do not eliminate the Electric weakness. Its recovery and typing offer different utility from Tentacruel and Lanturn, so raw BST is not a valid reason to buff it.
SKARMORY|Keep|3|85 HP, 140 Defense, Roost, hazards and either Sturdy or Iron Barbs are already generous. Keep 70 Sp. Def and 40 Sp. Atk. Iron Barbs chip must be assessed alongside hazards and Helmet, not as an isolated ability. No additional recovery or physical bulk is warranted initially.
HOUNDOOM|Keep|3|Dark/Fire, 110 Sp. Atk, Nasty Plot and Adaptability provide strong wallbreaking. Intimidate and custom Flash Fire offer alternatives. Keep 95 Speed and 50 Defense; a Speed buff would remove a principal cost. Test supported Adaptability Fire attacks before deciding it needs yet more special offense.
KINGDRA|Keep|3|Balanced 95 offenses/defenses, Water/Dragon, Swift Swim or Sniper and Dragon Dance already make it excellent. Keep 85 Speed outside rain. The rain sweeper and critical-hit builds have different requirements. Avoid adding recovery or a permanent Speed ability that would make its strong defensive typing essentially free.

PERSIAN_ALOLAN|Keep|3|115 Speed, Fur Coat or Prankster and Dark utility already establish strong support. Keep 70 Attack and 90 Sp. Atk. Fur Coat cannot also give priority status, and Dark resists enemy Prankster targeting. Test utility with the four-move limit before adding recovery or physical damage to match regular Persian.
GOLEM_ALOLAN|Keep|3|Galvanize converts strong Normal attacks into Electric STAB, while Magnet Pull offers a distinct trapping route. Keep 120 Attack, low Speed and the Ground weakness. Galvanize and trapping do not combine. Compare actual converted attacks and Ground counters before treating its awkward Rock/Electric typing as requiring a stat buff.
MUK_ALOLAN|Keep|3|Poison/Dark, 105 HP/Attack, 100 Sp. Def and Poison Puppeteer or Poison Touch give powerful defensive disruption. Keep stats and lack of Regenerator, which distinguishes regular Muk. Gluttony's implementation has limited benefit with this item set; it need not be replaced with another premium ability when two strong builds already exist.
EXEGGUTOR_ALOLAN|Keep|3|125 Attack, 105 Sp. Atk, Grass/Dragon, Rock Head or Harvest and recovery create mixed slow offense. Keep 45 Speed and the Ice weakness. Regular Exeggutor's Chlorophyll is not inherited as an active final-form ability. Evaluate recoil-free attacks and Berry recovery separately before raising physical damage further.
MAROWAK_ALOLAN|Keep|3|Thick Club, Fire/Ghost, Rock Head Flare Blitz or Lightning Rod and Swords Dance already provide major offense or an immunity pivot. Keep Attack 80 and low Speed. Lightning Rod is a different build from recoil-free Rock Head. Its low 425 BST does not justify a raw Attack increase when Thick Club already doubles that stat.
PERRSERKER|Keep|3|110 Attack, 100 Defense, Tough Claws or Steely Spirit, Swords Dance and Bullet Punch give strong physical Steel offense. Keep 50 Speed and current bulk. Steely Spirit boosts Steel attacks even in this singles game, but does not also supply Tough Claws. Compare those actual sets before adding more Attack.
RAPIDASH_GALARIAN|Keep|3|The runtime Enhanced type is Fairy/Fire, with 105 Attack, 115 Speed, Morning Sun and custom Flash Fire. This is already a strong identity distinct from its main-game typing. Keep stats and coverage. Pastel Veil offers separate status protection; do not evaluate it as also absorbing Fire attacks.
SLOWBRO_GALARIAN|Watch|3|Poison/Psychic, 95 HP/Defense, mixed 100 offenses, Slack Off and Regenerator or Unaware already create a flexible tank. Keep stats. Evaluate physical and special attacks separately, including the engine's dynamic Shell Side Arm category. Do not assume all attacks always use the higher offense or add bulk to match both regular Slowbro roles.
SLOWKING_GALARIAN|Watch|2|110 Sp. Atk/Sp. Def, Poison/Psychic, hazards, Slack Off and Regenerator or Unaware form a very strong special pivot. Keep stats initially and test it alongside the regular Slowking against identical opponents. Its broader poison utility is a reason to avoid additional coverage or bulk, not a reason to buff all four Slow forms together.
WEEZING_GALARIAN|Keep|3|Poison/Fairy, 120 Defense, burns and Levitate or Neutralizing Gas provide distinctive defensive disruption. Keep stats and limited healing. SNEASLER|Nerf move chance|2|130 Attack, 120 Speed, Technician Mach Punch, Swords Dance and Dire Claw's 50% status chance create very high offensive disruption. This targets random disabling pressure while retaining a fast Fighting/Poison identity.
